title: OpenAI calls trade secret dispute ‘a mess of Apple’s own making’
snippet: Apple yesterday presented what it said was “shocking evidence” based on analysis of a MacBook owned by Chang Liu, a former employee who moved to OpenAI. The company is alleging that two of its former employees stole trade secrets relating to hardware design and more. The AI company hit back with its own legal filing, saying that the whole situation is “a mess of Apple’s own making” … more…
fullText:
Apple yesterday presented what it said was “shocking evidence” based on analysis of a MacBook owned by Chang Liu, a former employee who moved to OpenAI. The company is alleging that two of its former employees stole trade secrets relating to hardware design and more.

The AI company hit back with its own legal filing, saying that the whole situation is “a mess of Apple’s own making” …

The ongoing lawsuit is to determine whether Liu and Tang Tan stole confidential information acquired from their employment at Apple in order to help OpenAI develop an AI hardware device. In particular, it alleges that both engineers downloaded confidential engineering files after leaving the iPhone maker.

Apple was granted access to a MacBook belonging to Liu in order to carry out a forensic analysis to determine whether it held evidence of unlawful access to the company’s intellectual property. The firm yesterday submitted a court filing claiming it had found four “shocking” pieces of evidence backing its allegations.

In its own filing made the same day, Reuters reports that OpenAI doesn’t hold back.

Employees “can leave a company like Apple that has struggled to ⁠adopt ​AI and move to an exciting startup that builds innovative products,” ​OpenAI wrote. “Apple may not like those choices. But it cannot claim those choices are unlawful, and it cannot use its own sloppy ​procedures to blame others for its own mess.”

	

Specifically, it says the problems were caused by three issues:

Apple encourages employees to use personal iCloud accounts to access Apple documents

Departing employees aren’t given enough time to return company devices, transfer files back to the company, and hand over responsibilities

Former employees are contacted by their erstwhile team members for assistance after they have left, requiring them to access company information

9to5Mac’s Take

On the face of it, the evidence Apple provided yesterday does appear damning. OpenAI doesn’t seem to be denying that confidential Apple information was used by the company, but rather claiming that the iPhone maker failed to properly protect it.

However, while I’m not a lawyer, my understanding is that this could become a crucial argument – since companies can only claim information comprises a trade secret if they have taken appropriate steps to protect it. If OpenAI can show that Apple did not do so, then the AI company could prevail even if use of the information is proven.

title: Samsung’s Android 17-based One UI 9 beta expands to these Galaxy phones this month
snippet: Samsung is expanding its Android 17 / One UI 9 beta program to several new Galaxy smartphones this month, signaling that the stable release isn’t too far away. more…
fullText:
Samsung is expanding its Android 17 / One UI 9 beta program to several new Galaxy smartphones this month, signaling that the stable release isn’t too far away.

One UI 9, based on Android 17, is live out of the box on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series and the Flip 8, but it’s yet to roll out to the broader Galaxy ecosystem. Galaxy S26 users have been able to test the update in beta for the past few months, but it’s only now that the beta is expanding.

Samsung has confirmed that the One UI 9 beta is now expanding to the company’s 2025 flagship lineups, including:

Galaxy S25/+/Ultra/FE

Galaxy Z Fold 7

Galaxy Z Flip 7

The update will be available as an opt-in beta through the Samsung Members app in India, Korea, the US, and the UK “in September.” While there’s no concrete timeline, it’s likely to be sooner than later based on past releases.

	

Samsung says:

Following the expansion of the One UI 9 beta with the Galaxy S26 series in May, the program will roll out to more devices starting in September. Eligible devices include Galaxy Z Fold7, Galaxy Z Flip7, Galaxy S25, Galaxy S25+, Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 FE. The program will be available in select markets, including India, Korea, the U.K. and the U.S. Users can sign up to participate through the Samsung Members app.

title: Google’s Gemini Spark can now manage your Google Photos library
snippet: Gemini Spark can edit and curate photo albums, create shared collections, turn photos into calendar events, and handle other Google Photos tasks for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
fullText:
Google is integrating more of its services with AI, as the company announced that its personal agent, Gemini Spark, can now manage your Google Photos library. That means you can ask Gemini Spark to execute tasks in Google Photos, like editing images, curating albums, automatically creating shared albums with your favorite shots, turning concert flyer photos into calendar appointments, running workflows, and more. 

On Thursday evening, Google Photos lead Shimrit Ben-Yair shared the new capabilities in a post on X, noting that the new capabilities would roll out over the next few weeks to eligible Gemini AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the U.S. in English.

The company didn’t say if or when it would roll out more broadly to international markets.

For a while now, I’ve relied on @GeminiApp and @antigravity agents across a wide range of use cases—spanning creativity, productivity, and analysis. But I’ve always dreamed of having a power agent to help me get the most out of my 143,206 photos and videos. And that day has come!… pic.twitter.com/WbnkYpattQ

— shimrit ben-yair (@shimritby) September 3, 2026

The addition is yet another example of Google attempting to find product-market fit in terms of making AI appealing to consumers — in this case, by automating tedious tasks and helping people manage what are now often sizable photo libraries.

The move comes at a time when the AI industry is reckoning with the fact that it hasn’t properly sold the promise of AI to consumers. This week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bloomberg that the industry has “done a terrible job” communicating the benefits of technology, which has led to backlash from communities around the world.

Announcements like this from Google are part of the problem. While they may make certain tasks easier, on their own, such features don’t seem revolutionary or even, really, necessary. (It’s not that difficult to make a photo album after all.) But the competitive nature of the AI industry is pushing companies to promote every AI-infused upgrade, no matter how small, instead of waiting until the company can tell a broader story about how AI has shaped its software for the better. 

To use Gemini Spark with Google Photos, you’ll need to first connect Google Photos to Gemini, then toggle on Spark in the top corner of the Gemini app, and enter your prompt.

If you’re a Netflix subscriber, you’re also paying for a huge catalog of great iPhone and iPad games. more…

fullText:
The monthly “Google System Release Notes” primarily detail what’s new in Play services, Play Store, and Play system update across Android phones/tablets, Wear OS, Google/Android TV, Auto, and PC. Some features apply to end users, while others are aimed at developers.

Private Compute Services: App info

Quick Share Extension

Settings Services: App info

SIM Manager: App info

System parental controls: App info

To update, open the Settings app > tap your name at the very top for “Google services” (on Pixel) > All services tab > Privacy & security > System services.

A feature appearing in the changelog does not mean it’s widely available. Some capabilities take months to fully launch.

[Phone, TV, Wear] Parents and teens can more easily set up Google Play account supervision and complete required age attestation.

Developer Services

System Management

title: Motorola is finally making a new Wear OS watch and it’s not called the Moto 360
snippet: It’s finally happening. Motorola is making a new Wear OS smartwatch, but it’s not a new Moto 360 – this is the Moto Watch Ultra. more…
fullText:
It’s finally happening. Motorola is making a new Wear OS smartwatch, but it’s not a new Moto 360 – this is the Moto Watch Ultra.

Rewinding the clock, the Moto 360 is perhaps still the most iconic Android smartwatch of all time. It was the poster child for the early days of “Android Wear,” but Motorola threw in the towel after a couple of generations. There was a brief revival of the Moto 360 name in 2020, but even that faded away – and the licensing deal behind it is likely why Motorola isn’t using that name now.

Motorola hasn’t stopped making smartwatches in that time, but they’ve all been based on an RTOS, making them fall into the category of smartwatches that are focused on health tracking and battery life at the expense of more useful notifications and access to a proper app ecosystem. The most recent attempt ended up cloning Wear OS’ design, despite the limitations.

Now, Motorola has a new smartwatch – the Moto Watch Ultra.

	

The $349 smartwatch offers up a Snapdragon W5+ Gen 1 chipset, 2GB of RAM, and 32GB of storage, all used to power Wear OS 6. We’ll have to wait and see if Motorola has made any customizations to the UI here, but re-entering the Wear OS ecosystem is a pretty big deal. Motorola does note that its Qira AI assistant is on board.

The Ultra has a 1.5-inch pOLED display in a 46mm chassis that’s 12.1mm thick – though Motorola’s images make it seem a lot thicker. The display is covered in Gorilla Glass 3 and the body is stainless steel with a brushed finish in silver or gunmetal finishes. There are four strap options, including both silicone and leather, but you can use any 22mm band as there are no fancy connectors, just a traditional spring pin. There’s NFC support for Google Wallet, IP68 + 5ATM dust/water resistance, and LTE support too. Motorola claims 2 days of use from the 550 mAh battery inside – Pixel Watch 5 (45mm) has a 465 mAh battery, for comparison. Charging is handled by a magnetic dock that connects over USB-C.

On the fitness side, Motorola is working with Polar – another brand that tried and has since left the Wear OS market – with features including activity goals, scores, and intensity zones, as well as inactivity alerts, energy sources, and wellness features around breathing and sleep. 

The Moto Watch Ultra will be available unlocked starting on September 10 for $349, with a debut on Verizon on September 24. Other carriers including T-Mobile, Metro, and AT&T will follow later on. 

Beyond the Watch Ultra, Motorola is today also launching a Swarovski version of the base Razr (2026). This special release has the same specs, but with a new dark grey case that has Crystals by Swarovski embedded in the back. It also costs $100 more at $899 and is also launching on September 10.

title: No little kids allowed, and other new info about Tesla’s Cybercab
snippet: The company says no children under 13 can ride -- even with a parent. That's more restrictive than the Model Y SUVs it's using as robotaxis.
fullText:
Tesla’s private Cybercab event has come and gone, and it was very different from the large, loud, livestreamed events the company usually puts on — an odd choice for the launch of a product CEO Elon Musk has spent years building toward.  

In fact, it doesn’t even appear that Musk spoke at the event, the keynote of which, by all accounts, only lasted around 15 minutes.

The promise of the Cybercab is massive: a fully autonomous vehicle that uses only cameras and AI to drive itself, all for much less than a Waymo. But Tesla scattered a lot of the details. Some are in PDFs the company released on Thursday, as well as in updated terms of service in its “Robotaxi” app. The rest were left for a select few die-hard fans to disseminate online.  

The company now has to prove that these vehicles are safe — to the public, to local governments, and to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, which has already opened an investigation into Tesla’s Cybercab rollout.  

In the meantime, here are some of the most interesting new details that caught our attention: 

No Cybercab for kiddos

One of the more interesting details in the Cybercab fine print is that Tesla does not allow minors under the age of 13 to ride in the vehicle “at this time.”  

Minors between the ages of 8 and 17 are allowed to ride in Tesla’s “Robotaxi” Model Y SUVs, and Tesla does have guidelines on how to use child seats in both vehicles. 

Curiously, the Cybercab does not have the standard LATCH anchors for child seats. Instead, they can only be attached using the seat belt. Tesla executives, including Musk, have talked a lot about how much they focus on taking out unnecessary parts to cut down on costs, though I’ll admit I wasn’t expecting the company to ditch child seat anchors — especially given Musk’s obsession with making more babies. 

All children under 18 must be accompanied by an adult in both vehicles, according to Tesla. But something is making Tesla hesitate on allowing young children in the Cybercab for now. 

What happens in a crash? 

While the goal of an autonomous vehicle is to avoid crashing, even the most capable ones on the road today do wind up in collisions. 

Here’s what happens when the Cybercab gets in a crash: The airbags will inflate, the doors will unlock, the hazard warning lights and interior lights will turn on, the high voltage battery is disabled, the windows go to the “vent” position, the Cybercab will apply the brakes to come to a stop and park, and the infotainment system will start up a two-way connection with Tesla’s rider support team. 

Unlocking the doors is notable because Tesla has come under fire for its reliance on electronic door latches, both in its home market of the United States and in its largest market, China. Just last month, Tesla agreed to recall 3 million cars in China, alongside a number of other automakers, as a result of an investigation into electronic door latches that could trap people following a crash.  

Manual door releases

Speaking of doors, another recent criticism of Tesla is that its interior manual door releases are too hard to find in an emergency. These are necessary because the electronic door latches are the main method of getting in and out of the company’s vehicles, activated either by pushing a button or using a smartphone.  

The Cybercab uses electronic door latches, which allow the doors to open automatically at the start or end of a ride. There is also a small button on the exterior of the car that riders can use to open the doors. But inside, the manual release is thankfully in a very obvious spot on the armrest of each door.  

Brake-by-wire

Tesla is using a brake-by-wire system in the Cybercab, again largely (it seems) for the purposes of cutting costs. Instead of using a hydraulic system that pumps fluid through lines to control brake pressure, Tesla has electronic actuators controlling the brake calipers. 

“Having electric brakes avoids the complexity of a hydraulic system: no need to rout [sic] plumbing all around the car,” Musk wrote in a post. 

The company was already the first major automaker to use steer-by-wire on its Cybertruck, severing the physical connection between the steering wheel and the front wheels.

A little fresh air

For some reason, the windows of the Cybercab “cannot be fully opened at this time.” Tesla doesn’t explain why in the documentation it released this week. 

USB-C power

According to influencer Jeremy Judkins, the USB-C outlets in the Cybercab put out 90W of power — roughly four times more than you’d typically find inside a car.

Sean O’Kane is a reporter who has spent a decade covering the rapidly-evolving business and technology of the transportation industry, including Tesla and the many startups chasing Elon Musk. Most recently, he was a reporter at Bloomberg News where he helped break stories about some of the most notorious EV SPAC flops. He previously worked at The Verge, where he also covered consumer technology, hosted many short- and long-form videos, performed product and editorial photography, and once nearly passed out in a Red Bull Air Race plane.

title: Dyson Went Bonkers During IFA 2026: Here Are all 10 of Its New Products
snippet: Dyson popped off at a launch event in Berlin, introducing a whopping 10 new products.
fullText:
Gone are the days when Dyson, one of the biggest names in home and beauty tech, let new products trickle out to the masses. 

It was a slow burn at first, and for years, the brand made only vacuums, fans and air purifiers. In 2016, beauty tech, including cult-favorite hair care tools like the Supersonic hair dryer and Airwrap, was folded into the lineup. Still, we’d be lucky to see a handful of new stuff released each year.

Those days are over.

This year during IFA, the massive Euro tech showcase, Dyson has gone off, as the kids say, and released a whopping 10 new products at its counterprogramming event in Berlin, dubbed “Dyson Unveiled.” From floor care and air purifiers to health and beauty tech, including its first-ever toothbrush, Dyson’s eye-popping launch is matched only by last year when the brand introduced 11 new products.

Dyson is tackling oral care with the release of a camera-equipped toothbrush and a water flosser.Dyson

Dyson isn’t just churning out products at a faster rate, as Dyson’s Chief Engineer Jake Dyson explained. 

“The latest innovations combine Dyson’s decades of mechanical engineering with AI, vision systems and machine learning to create products that can see, understand and respond to the environments around them,” he said.

Our team on the ground got a close-up look at everything the brand has coming to market, and the list is long. Here’s what’s new from Dyson in 2026.

CameraJet toothbrush 

At IFA 2026, we’re seeing all the upgraded, AI-powered, repairable, camera-equipped tech. And then some.Tara Brown/CNET

This is Dyson’s first toothbrush, and it houses a tiny camera for the most detailed possible cleaning. According to the brand, it’s the first oral care tool to use AI-powered vision to detect and target gaps between teeth. It brushes, liquid flosses and even dispenses mouthwash. 

The toothbrush costs $499 and is available now.

Dyson Airsmooth dryer brush

Dyson has unveiled its first-ever dryer brush.Tara Brown/CNET

Dyson’s releases aren’t limited to air care and cleaning. The brand released its first-ever dedicated dryer brush, which uses smart heat control and novel dual-bristle technology to dry, smooth and lift hair all in one motion. 

The Airsmooth will retail for $249 and will be available to order starting on Sept. 8.

Dyson Corrale CoolShine straightener

Tara Brown/CNET

The success of Dyson’s cult-favorite Airwrap inspired this next-generation straightening tool, featuring flexing plates with active cooling that dries hair without exposing it to as much heat, as heat can damage hair.

The Corrale CoolShine costs $329 and hits shelves on Sept. 15.

HushJet Pure Cool Plus Formaldehyde air purifier

Dyson’s new HushJet air purifiers are a total redesign.Tara Brown/CNET

This new compact high-performance purifier and fan is designed for large spaces. The brand says it delivers three times the power of its predecessors. You can grab this model in the fall for $599.

HushJet Big Plus Quiet Cool Pure Plus Formaldehyde air purifier

Dyson’s new HushJet Big Cool has an angled pipe design and a rotating mouth. Dyson

Dyson’s most powerful purifier is engineered for long-range air projection and multiroom purification. It has a three-stage filtration system that captures particulates and gases, and it destroys formaldehyde.

This model will cost a whopping $1,099 and hits retailers in the fall.

HushJet Hot Cool Pure Plus air purifier

Dyson’s most powerful three-in-one purifier was on display in Berlin.Tara Brown/CNET

Dyson’s most powerful three-in-one purifier combines purification, heating and personal cooling in one machine for year-round home comfort.

This also launches in the fall and retails for $599.

Read our full coverage of Dyson’s new HushJet lineup here.

R3 Nurovi Spot Plus Scrub UV 

Dyson is calling the R3 Nurovi Spot Plus Scrub UV its most advanced robot vacuum to date.Dyson

The brand is calling this its most advanced wet-and-dry robot vacuum to date. It features UV enhancement and, you guessed it, AI elements to help identify up to 200 types of stains and substances. The self-cleaning wet roller uses a 12-point system that continuously applies water heated to 158 degrees Fahrenheit to simultaneously lift and remove stubborn stains.

The robot vac costs $1,199 and is available starting Sept. 15.

R1 Nurovi Dry

Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry robot vacuum cleaner.

The Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry is engineered for deep cleaning on hard floors and carpets. It uses Dyson’s Twin-capture technology and intelligent floor and dust sensing. 

This simpler robot vac will be available sometime in September for $549.

R2 Nurovi Wash Plus Dry 

Dyson’s R2 Nurovi Wash Plus Dry robot vacuum.

Another robot vac is joining the lineup. This one has triangular cleaning pads to clean those pesky room corners.

The Wash Plus Dry is now available exclusively at Costco for $699.

W1 PencilWash Plus Dok

The PencilWash weighs less than 5 pounds and is just as thin as the PencilVac.

Dyson

The new handheld cleaner is slimmer and lighter than the older model, includes a more absorbent roller and a hygienic waste system. It also has self-cleaning features built into the dock.

It will cost $349 and will be available in the fall.

title: Instagram cracking down on accounts that feature AI-generated influencers
snippet: As AI slop continues to dominate the web, Instagram is cracking down on accounts that leverage AI-generated influencers by threatening to restrict their reach. more…
fullText:
As AI slop continues to dominate the web, Instagram is cracking down on accounts that leverage AI-generated influencers by threatening to restrict their reach.

In a blog post, Instagram details that its “AI creator” label for accounts is now going to say “AI-generated profile,” better reflecting that the account is not just using AI, but that viewers are interacting with an influencer that is entirely AI-generated. 

Accounts that were using the “AI creator” label will have a chance to review the status and have it removed if it no longer fits their content. 

The bigger change, though, is that Instagram will actively crack down on accounts that don’t use the label at all if they are using “AI-generated influencers.” This includes not showing content in recommendations such as the “For You” page. 

	

Instagram explains:

For unlabeled profiles that feature an AI-generated person, creators can and should apply the label by editing their profile and toggling on AI-generated profile. The label will then begin to appear on their profile and alongside their content if their specific media doesn’t already have a label indicating that it was created or edited with AI. Creators who proactively add the AI-generated profile label will not see a change to their profile’s reach.

Adding the label or appealing the decision can reverse the impact, but this is a considerable change on Instagram’s part, especially as AI-generated content has become incredibly prevelant on both Instagram and Facebook, both Meta-operated platforms.

snippet: As soon as next month, Apple is expected to introduce its next MacBook Pro redesign. We’ll be seeing OLED, the first touchscreen on a Mac, a thinner chassis, Dynamic Island, and much more. This upgrade was rumored to be called MacBook Ultra, though it wasn’t necessarily clear where that’d leave the MacBook Pro brand. Now, it’s a lot more clear. more…
fullText:
As soon as next month, Apple is expected to introduce its next MacBook Pro redesign. We’ll be seeing OLED, the first touchscreen on a Mac, a thinner chassis, Dynamic Island, and much more. This upgrade was rumored to be called MacBook Ultra, though it wasn’t necessarily clear where that’d leave the MacBook Pro brand. Now, it’s a lot more clear.

At first, one would’ve assumed that the base model 14″ MacBook Pro with the M5 chip would fulfill the MacBook Pro moniker. Then, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple would also be bringing certain elements of the MacBook Ultra design to the base MacBook Pro with M7. To me, this made the idea of ‘MacBook Ultra’ branding much less likely.

Now, a new report makes the idea of both MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra much more sensible in the lineup.

According to Omdia, Apple will be keeping the current miniLED display panels in production through 2028.

This means two things: for one, if the existing MacBook Pro is staying in the lineup, the redesigned model will likely come with a significant price premium. It also means that the new model is much more likely to be called MacBook Ultra.

So, over the course of the next ~year, the MacBook lineup will likely look like this:

Fall 2026:

MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)

MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M5)

MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch, M6)

MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

MacBook Ultra (OLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

Spring 2027:

MacBook Neo (A19 Pro)

MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M6)

MacBook Pro (OLED, 14-inch, M7)

MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

MacBook Ultra (OLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

Wrap up

If all comes to fruition, the MacBook lineup will be bigger than ever. Ultimately, the older MacBook Pro remaining in the lineup will probably be short lived. I imagine it’s part of Apple’s strategy to keep the starting prices lower, as the company has done in the past. 

In this scenario, I could see the miniLED MacBook Pros remaining around at $2499 starting, whereas the Ultra starts even higher, perhaps $2999.

title: Where Google Wallet state IDs are available on Android
snippet: States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android. more…
fullText:
States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android.

Update 9/5

How to add your state ID on Android

Open the Google Wallet app on Android 9+

Tap the “plus” button next to “View more” at the bottom

Choose “ID & personal info” and then “Driver’s license or state ID” 

Select your state and follow the instructions

The process involves taking a picture of the front and back of your physical card, as well as a short video of yourself for verification: a “photo from this video will be submitted to your ID issuer.” 

Once approved, the ID will appear below the carousel of payment methods alongside other passes. The order can be rearranged, while you can remotely remove the ID online if your phone is missing: myaccount.google.com > Personal Info > Manage IDs.

	

What Google Wallet state IDs are supported

Arizona (Rolled out October 2023)

Arkansas (Rolled out October 2025)

California (Rolled out August 2024)

Colorado (Rolled out October 2023)

Georgia (Rolled out October 2023)

Iowa (Rolled out June 2025)

Maryland (Rolled out December 2022)

Montana (Rolled out August 2025)

New Mexico (Rolled out December 2024)

North Dakota (Rolled out October 2025)

[New] Ohio (Rolled out September 2026)

Puerto Rico (Rolled out October 2025)

Where state IDs are coming next

Google previously said to expect support in the following places:

West Virginia (Upcoming availability announced April 2025)

Where you can use state IDs

The primary place you can use this digital ID is at TSA checkpoints in some US airports. There are two ways to do so, starting with tapping your phone at the NFC terminal. You then review the information that will be shared with the TSA and authenticate with device unlock. There’s also a QR code method that requires opening the ID in Google Wallet. 

Officially, you still have to carry the physical ID card at all times.

Some apps, like from car rental services, are beginning to accept digital IDs for identity and age verification. On mobile, if an app or website requests your age, it’s as simple as confirming (and authenticating) that you want to share this information with a system-level prompt/sheet. On desktop web, the experience involves scanning a QR code. 

Google wants to make it possible to do that “without any possibility to link back to a user’s personal identity” through what it calls Zero-Knowledge Proof. This technology will be open-sourced for anyone to use. 

Looking ahead, the IDs can be used at DMVs in Arizona, Georgia, Maryland, and New Mexico as part of “improved and streamlined customer experiences.”

	

Google is also working on letting you use digital IDs to “recover Amazon accounts, access online health services with CVS and MyChart by Epic, verify profiles on platforms like Uber and more.”

Using passport as REAL ID

Google in April pointed out how you can “use your ID pass created from a U.S. passport with TSA security for domestic travel at supported airports, even if you do not have a REAL ID driver’s license or state-issued ID.” This comes ahead of the May 7, 2025 deadline. 

To do so, open Google Wallet > Add to Wallet > ID pass. This three-step process involves taking a picture of your passport’s info page, and then scanning the security chip found inside the back cover of your passport. You also have to record a video of your face that Google will review “to make sure you’re a real person, and compare the video to your passport photo to make sure you’re the owner of the passport.”

The NFC and QR code instructions for using this digital passport ID are unchanged from above. You also have to keep the physical version on you when traveling. As a reminder, this won’t work internationally.

title: HomeKit Weekly: ULTRALOQ’s Bolt Fingerprint has everything you’d want except Home Key
snippet: My door has had a smart lock on it for 5-6 years, and I’ve tried plenty of options. The ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a great option for almost anyone thanks to its Apple Home integration, built-in Wi-Fi, and plenty of ways to lock and unlock your door. Whether you’re looking for fingerprint ID unlock or a simple PIN, this lock has almost everything. more…
fullText:
My door has had a smart lock on it for 5-6 years, and I’ve tried plenty of options. The ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a great option for almost anyone thanks to its Apple Home integration, built-in Wi-Fi, and plenty of ways to lock and unlock your door. Whether you’re looking for fingerprint ID unlock or a simple PIN, this lock has almost everything.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ calls the Bolt Fingerprint its first smart lock fully integrated into Apple Home, and that integration is the major selling point for me. To be honest, I still miss Touch ID on my iPhone. You can lock and unlock the door from the Home app or with Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV as a hub, it works in automations and remote control just like any other Apple Home accessory with scene and automation support. 

That said, there’s one feature still missing for me: Home Key support. The ability to simply tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to unlock the door would take this lock to the next level. It’s literally the only thing missing, but it’s not a dealbreaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ considers adding this in a future model, because with Home Key, this lock could go from great to nearly perfect. The lock also works with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so you have flexibility regardless of your preferred smart home platform or what it might change to down the road. It runs on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, so you don’t need a separate bridge for basic remote control via their app. 

More ways to get in than you will ever need

The Bolt Fingerprint is not shy about unlock options, either. The fingerprint ID stores up to 50 fingers and up to 50 passcodes, app unlock from your phone, auto-unlock when you walk up to the door, and voice unlock through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys are included as well, so you’re never fully locked out if the batteries are dead, etc. Not having physical keys is a non-starter for me.

You can also create up to 50 custom passcodes and hand out one-time or scheduled codes to friends, guests, cleaners, etc. If you rent out a house, this alone makes it worth a look.

There’s also a Lockout Mode that temporarily disables every electronic unlock method, including passcodes and app access, for anyone heading out of town who wants an extra layer of security while the house sits empty. I hadn’t considered this a feature in a smart lock, but it’s not a bad one to have.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I’ve installed enough smart deadbolts over the past few years to know what I’m doing at this point. I can do it in around ten minutes, assuming I have my tools handy. There is no wiring or drilling required, assuming you are replacing a modern deadbolt. All you need is a Phillips head screwdriver, and you’ll also need to replace the strike plate on your door.

Once the lock is scanned into your Apple Home environment and assigned to a room, you can control it from the Home app, or add it to automations and scenes so multiple actions trigger together, as your lights turn on the moment the door unlocks, etc.

Wrap up on ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint

Overall, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a great choice for anyone who doesn’t require Home Key support. The fingerprint unlock is likely to become your go-to option for day-to-day use. Installation is easy. I’ve been using it on my office door for a while now, as I often have laptops waiting to be deployed in boxes that I want additional security for. I love how it unlocks as I get closer, and I love the logistics of tracking who has come and gone. The fingerprint support reminds me of the good old Touch ID days. 

You can buy the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint from Amazon or directly from ULTRALOQ.

title: Dropbox breach seemingly caused by egregious authentication failure [U]
snippet: Multiple Dropbox users have been emailed by the cloud storage company to advise them that a security breach saw unauthorised access to their account. Update: the company has said that about 5,000 accounts were compromised, with files downloaded from around 1,500 of them. The root cause appears to be a lack of authentication by Dropbox when attackers created a single sign-on option through a third-party company … more…
fullText:
Multiple Dropbox users have been emailed by the cloud storage company to advise them that a security breach saw unauthorised access to their account. Update: the company has said that about 5,000 accounts were compromised, with files downloaded from around 1,500 of them.

The root cause appears to be a lack of authentication by Dropbox when attackers created a single sign-on option through a third-party company … 

Developer Yoni Levy posted a copy of the email he received on X.

We are writing to let you know that we’ve observed unauthorized access to your Dropbox account between August 4 and August 21, 2026. While our logs show no evidence that your files were viewed or downloaded, we want to share with you what happened, what we are doing about it, and what additional steps you can take.

Other Dropbox users reported receiving the same email in which the company said it resulted from a problem with a single sign-on (SSO) option using Lenovo IDs.

Dropbox partners with Lenovo as an identity provider so that users can log in to their Dropbox accounts using verified Lenovo IDs. While you may not have an existing Lenovo ID, our investigation determined that an issue with Lenovo’s email verification process allowed an unauthorized party to register a Lenovo ID using your email address and then use that Lenovo ID to log into the Dropbox account associated with that email address.

However, while Dropbox claims the flaw was in Lenovo’s email verification process, the bigger issue appears to be that Dropbox itself did not require users to use their existing login to verify the new SSO, as The CyberSec Guru reports.

Recon/selection: The attacker compiles target email addresses (breach corpora, LinkedIn, customer lists — email addresses are effectively public data).

Rogue IdP enrollment: The attacker registers a Lenovo ID as victim@example.com. No inbox access is needed because Lenovo’s verification step is missing or bypassable. The display name is set to something disposable — one victim who reclaimed the rogue account found the name “John Madden,” the late NFL broadcaster, a strong tell of bulk, low-effort registration.

Federated sign-in: The attacker clicks “Continue with Lenovo” on Dropbox. Lenovo’s authorization server issues a token whose email claim matches the victim’s Dropbox account.

Implicit account linking: Dropbox resolves the email claim to the existing account and mints a session. No password prompt, no step-up, no “link this new identity?” consent. From Dropbox’s perspective, a trusted IdP had already vouched for the address.

9to5Mac’s Take

While there was certainly a failure to verify email addresses at the Lenovo end, it would not have done any harm if Dropbox had authenticated the linked ID before it could be used to sign in. Failing to do so is an egregious fault.

The company has now fixed the flaw and expired all sessions previously ‘authenticated’ through a Lenovo ID.

If you don’t already have two-factor authentication enabled for Dropbox, it is highly recommended to change this immediately.

Between this brute's spacious … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Thanks to their ability to provide a smooth ride and quiet powertrain with ease, electric vehicles are a true shoo-in for the high-end luxury automotive segment. Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac’s Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne.

I recently got a quick ride in a heavily camouflaged preproduction Torcal as a way to experience it before its official debut toward the end of this month. Between this brute’s spacious interior, supple ride quality, and focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, all signs point to it not just being a viable competitor in the segment, but also characteristically Bentley.

When I say heavily camouflaged, this not only covers (pun intended) the Torcal’s exterior, but the interior as well. Thick black cloth was draped over most of it, to the point of the engineers punching holes in the cloth for proper seatbelt usage. The exterior was rather deceiving, too; apparently they affixed false body paneling under the wrap so as not to fully spoil its overall shape and profile. Upon first glance, it seemed like Bentley took a page from Lucid’s Gravity by making it wider at the front than at the back—in the name of teardrop-resembling aerodynamics—but Martin Page, the Torcal’s product line director-slash-chauffeur for my ride, assured me that what I was seeing (or rather, trying to see) wouldn’t be production.

1/6

However, this enabled me to zero in closer on what I could feel and hear. Whether up front or in back, the Torcal is amply spacious, even though it’s noticeably smaller in size and shape than Bentley’s current Bentayga. Page explained the great lengths that engineers reached to ensure it had an isolating and tremendously smooth ride. Running off-the-shelf two-chamber air suspension — common in the rest of the brand’s lineup — would seemingly suffice with an EV’s inherently good chassis balance, but engineers took it a step further by carefully altering the flow of oil through its adaptive dampers. This means that the jump in ride and handling between Comfort and Sport modes is much more discernible. No matter the mode, it rode incredibly smoothly. Heavy focus was paid to the Torcal’s alignment, too, with steering that returns to and maintains center as confidently as possible.

Diving deeper into signature Bentley characteristics, developing the best simulated engine note was high on the list of priorities. Inspiration came from the brand’s V8-powered Turbo R of the 1980s, except the track itself was recorded by a musician’s drum beat and mixed accordingly, rather than simply churned out from a synthesizer.

“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects,” Page shared.

“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects.”

— Martin Page, Torcal’s product line director

The reasoning behind this lies in hearing subtle imperfections, much like one would from an analogue internal combustion powertrain. Going one step further, the Torcal’s throttle tuning seemed to mimic a torquey V8 with progressive power delivery. In light of this, Page added that with this sound turned on, it gives occupants auditory cues to tie to the vehicle’s torque delivery, which is known to help reduce motion sickness. The sound has not yet been finalized and is still being finely tweaked at the time of this writing.

I got a peek at the digital instrument cluster and center infotainment screen — Page had to observe the speed limit, after all. The image these display in the background is of a fine crystal decanter hand-cut by Cumbria Crystal with light shone through it. In Page’s words, this shows the natural refractions and reflections that you get from every one of the cuts. It’s another indication of the brand’s focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, albeit a subtle one.

It’s also worth pointing out that Bentley takes net environmental impact seriously. “In this car we take sustainability to another level, we have clear targets for circular material and green aluminum,” Page shared. “The door cards are made with a natural fiber — not injection-molded plastic — that’s fully recyclable and fully sustainable.”

Then, Bentley is working with fellow UK company Fox Brothers to offer a Merino wool interior option, not just as a lesser-taken route for comfort (Volvo’s done well with wool, too) but also as a sturdy, renewable material that will hold up to automotive use. Finally, the assembly plant in Crewe, England, has tough requirements for green energy use (namely solar) and other renewable practices.

Output, battery, and charging specs are not carved into stone just yet. Power will be north of 800 hp and 700 lb ft of torque, and curb weight is estimated to be nearly 6,000 lbs. Page was quiet about battery size (though, expect it to mirror the Porsche’s 108 net kWh unit), and the targeted range is over 370 miles. With a peak charging rate of 400 kW, the brand is aiming for a 10–80 percent top-up in under 20 minutes, with 100 miles tacking on in as little as seven.

“We’re trying to be authentic in the whole experience,” Page summed up as we headed back to the parking lot where I met him.

The approach with the Torcal is to make a great Bentley first, and in the process of doing so, a great EV. It combines some already hashed-out tech from Volkswagen, but the brand is hoping its focus on craftsmanship and fine-tuning will attract discerning, well-heeled potential customers who want an electric luxury vehicle. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet, but it will be interesting to see how the Torcal is received after its full official unveiling.

Images by Bentley

title: CD sales are making an unexpected comeback amid a retro tech boom
snippet: U.S. CD revenue jumped 58.6% in the first half of 2026, reversing last year’s decline as interest in retro tech and physical media continues to grow.
fullText:
Retro tech is making a comeback, and this week, the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) put hard numbers to that trend in terms of music consumption habits. Surprisingly, the organization reported that CDs — yes, the shiny, round things that Spotify supposedly killed — are growing once again.

According to the RIAA’s new report, CDs generated $171.1 million in revenue during the first half of 2026 — up 58.6% from roughly $107.9 million in the first half of 2025 — on 17.5 million units sold, up 45.7% from about 12 million units in the same period last year.

That rebound is all the more interesting because it follows a rough 2025. Last year’s full-year report showed CD revenue had actually fallen 7.8% for the full year, from $338.9 million in 2024 to $312.4 million in 2025, while units sold dropped 11.6%, from 33.3 million to 29.5 million.

The growth comes amid a surge of renewed interest in simpler tech, like so-called dumbphones, digital cameras, typewriters, landlines, and physical media like CDs and vinyl, among other categories. For Gen Z, the demand for these devices represents a sort of yearning for an era of tech they never got to experience — where you had more control over when you engaged with technology and how, and tech itself had less room to invade your life with its notifications, addictive apps, and algorithms.

Several startups are playing in this space now, too, including landline makers like Tin Can, Ooma, and Pinwheel, and non-smartphones like those from Light, Dumb Co, Minimal, and others, including the soon-to-launch BlackBerry-like Clicks. Meanwhile, Gen Z consumers are snapping up old gadgets at thrift stores or on vintage tech websites like eBay or Retrospekt.

And to be fair, the trend could be bigger than the RIAA’s numbers demonstrate, as they don’t include used CD sales, like those discs bought from thrift bins or garage sales, nor do they account for how many CDs have now been handed down from Gen X parents to their kids.

We should note there’s one caveat to the trend here. 

The RIAA changed how it calculates dollar figures in 2025, switching from estimated retail value to wholesale value. That means the 2024 and 2025 revenue numbers aren’t directly comparable. But unit sales, which aren’t affected by that change, tell the same fundamental story: 29.5 million CDs sold in 2025, down from 33.3 million in 2024. So CDs were still declining before this year’s unexpected rebound.

Vinyl sales continue to grow, too. In fact, so-called physical media revenue in the first half of 2026 jumped 25.9% to $731.5 million, driven ⁠not only by the 58.6% increase in CD revenue but also by a 17.7% increase in vinyl revenue.

title: New iPhone 18 Pro report details flagship camera feature and more
snippet: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be unveiled next week, and a new report offers fresh details on the flagship “mechanical aperture” camera feature that’s coming, plus mentions an improved vapor chamber and more. more…
fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be unveiled next week, and a new report offers fresh details on the flagship “mechanical aperture” camera feature that’s coming, plus mentions an improved vapor chamber and more.

Here’s what’s coming with iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, per Mark Gurman

Today Mark Gurman at Bloomberg published his latest expectations for the new iPhones being introduced on September 9.

While most of the report covers features reported previously, a few noteworthy details stand out.

For example, Apple has a new “mechanical aperture” camera feature coming to iPhone 18 Pro Max—and possibly the smaller iPhone 18 Pro too.

Despite plenty of reporting on this camera upgrade, which has also been called “variable aperture,” there have been minimal details on what it will enable. But Gurman reports today that it will be “for fine-tuning light adjustments and depth control.”

Additionally, the new report says iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will have “better battery life and improved vapor chambers to prevent overheating.”

Battery improvements were already expected, but good to see confirmed. The mention of improved vapor chambers is a new detail, though.

Apple first debuted a vapor chamber in the iPhone last year with iPhone 17 Pro. It seems the company already has a second-generation version ready to go.

Finally, Gurman says “in-house C2 modems” are coming to iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. While this isn’t a new rumor, it’s worth highlighting because some reports have claimed Apple is sticking with Qualcomm modems again this year.

For more on what to expect from iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, see our coverage here.

title: This Android phone has a detachable action camera, coming to the US for $999
snippet: IFA 2026 is delivering a pretty wild new Android phone that’s not only rugged, but has a GoPro-like action camera built-in which can be detached and used for capturing footage on the fly. more…
fullText:
IFA 2026 is delivering a pretty wild new Android phone that’s not only rugged, but has a GoPro-like action camera built-in which can be detached and used for capturing footage on the fly.

The RugOne XSnap 7 Pro first appeared earlier this year, but is now making a splash with official pricing and release information at IFA. The device is landing on Kickstarter next week and will cost $999 when it arrives in the US in October – €1,099 in Europe.

This rugged device comes from Ulephone, a known brand for these ruggedized Android smartphones, with “RugOne” being a new sub-brand under the company. And, as per usual, it’s a chonky device with a 19.1mm profile, IP68/IP69K/MIL-STD-810H certifications, and no need for a case with its rugged, drop-resistant design. It has a 6.67-inch FHD+ display using Gorilla Glass Victus on top, runs on a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 chip with 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, and has a massive 9,300 mAh battery. It even has a 64MP night vision camera to back up its 50MP main sensor. 

But the claim to fame here is a built-in, detachable action camera.

	

The camera attaches to the phone magnetically with a 133-degree field-of-view and 2.7K (1440p) recording. It can record for 40 minutes on its built-in battery and has 64GB of storage for up to eight hours of storage, but a built-in app on the phone can let the camera use the phone’s storage to offload that footage, and the phone also recharges the camera. The app can let you stream from the camera from up to 50 meters away and the action camera is waterproof up to 5 meters with no additional equipment.

It’s a wild idea, and one that actually seems more compelling than most of these rugged devices. A clear bit of utility, decent specs, and even a promise of software support – it XSnap 7 Pro ships with Android 16 and is promised updates through Android 20. 

What do you think?

fullText:
Terrence O'Brien

 

is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Boox teased the Picco, its take on the buzzy Xteink X4 e-reader, back in July, but provided almost no details. Now, thanks to some reporting out of IFA, we’ve got a bit more info, though sadly still no price. Unlike the Xteink devices, the Picco will not have magnets on the back for attaching to a phone. The 3.97-inch e-paper display, however, will be touchscreen, which The Verge’s Andrew Liszewski called a “welcome upgrade” on the X4 Pro. The Picco has physical page-turn buttons, and they can be customized with different actions for short and long presses.

There’s apparently no onboard storage, and it relies entirely on a microSD card to hold books. But in addition to adding files to the card, you can transfer reading material to the Picco directly over USB-C (which the Xteink devices lack) or even WiFi from a companion app.

The Picco won’t run Android, like Boox’s other devices, and will instead run a stripped-down, Linux-based OS. The company is including a handful of additional apps like a timer, a todo list, and a reading stats tracker. But, it’s unlikely that Boox will open its firmware like Xteink has, so it might be a less hackable and customizable device.

There’s still some things we don’t know, like price, battery life, Bluetooth support, or if it will include a player for audiobooks. But all should be revealed in November, when it’s expected to launch.

title: Apple tells Mac App Store developers they can now drop Intel support
snippet: Apple started informing developers today that universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store that require macOS 13 or later can now drop support for Intel-based Macs. more…
fullText:
Apple started informing developers today that universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store that require macOS 13 or later can now drop support for Intel-based Macs.

In the email, Apple says:

We’re reaching out to let you know that universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store that require macOS 13 or later can now remove support for Intel-based Mac computers.

By removing support for Intel-based Mac computers, you can simplify your development and optimize your download and on-device size.

To remove Intel support, update your app build settings to “arm64” only. Then rebuild and submit your app to the Mac App Store.

Previously, developers were required to offer Intel compatibility. With today’s change, developers can drop support for Intel-based Macs. Intel users, however, can continue using the last version of the app compatible with their machine.

The changes come as macOS 27 Golden Gate drops support for Intel-powered Macs altogether. Apple also announced last year that Rosetta 2, the software that translates Intel apps for Apple Silicon, will be discontinued after macOS 27 (with some exceptions for for certain games).

fullText:
As the debut of Googlebook quietly approaches, a week full of new laptop launches at IFA continues to make me wonder why literally anyone should be even a tiny bit interested in Google’s new platform.

This issue of 9to5Google Weekender is a part of our newsletter that highlights the biggest Google stories with added commentary and more. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every weekend, and catch our weekday roundups too!

Googlebook made its debut earlier this year as the company’s Android-based desktop platform that will replace ChromeOS and, frankly, I’ve spent the last couple of months just sitting here stewing over the complete lack of information on what this platform is supposed to do and why anyone should care. Truly, I cannot remember the last time I was this skeptical about a Google product – is this how other people felt about Stadia?

At this point, not much has changed.

	

We’ve seen leaks of some of the first Googlebook laptops from Asus and Lenovo, while Acer was spotted teasing its Googlebook at IFA in Berlin. Some early apps have shown up too, including “Magic Pointer” which is the one new feature Google has actually shown off from this platform, a “Desktop Camera” app, and “Look up” which is in fact not a reference to that DiCaprio movie but instead an AI-powered experience that lets you interact with text to find relevant information such as definitions, flight tracking, and more. That one works on some Android phones, too. 

Yet, I still cannot fathom where Googlebooks fit into the larger market. ChromeOS had a clear selling point – stable and usable software on low-cost hardware, with later generations adding in some clever AI features and using more capable hardware. But where Googlebook might have been interesting from a cost perspective, a focus on “premium” hardware combined with RAMageddon and a sea of MacBook Neo competitors… I just don’t get it folks. 

The new IdeaPad Vibe from Lenovo and the Dell 14S were both announced this week as direct answers to Apple’s hit budget-conscious laptop, and Google is literally going in the opposite direction.

Damien laid out some potential ideas back in June, such as a focus on AI-aided vibe coding, but it’s still hard to imagine Google’s pitch at this point. Windows laptops are getting more affordable in the wake of the MacBook Neo, and is anyone looking to spend money on tech they don’t need to right now? Maybe I’m just having trouble seeing the potential or the positives here, but I can’t remember the last time I was so sour on a potential new Google launch. 

What do you think?

title: M6 MacBook Pro: Three new upgrades launching this fall
snippet: Apple has a new M6 MacBook Pro launching this fall with a 14-inch screen and the current industrial design. Now that the M6 chip has officially been unveiled, here are three upgrades to expect from the new MacBook Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple has a new M6 MacBook Pro launching this fall with a 14-inch screen and the current industrial design. Now that the M6 chip has officially been unveiled, here are three upgrades to expect from the new MacBook Pro.

#1: Dual 16-core Neural Engine

If AI is in any way significant to your workflows—and with macOS 27, it will be for even more users—then the M6 MacBook Pro could be a big upgrade.

That’s because the M6 chip includes a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, up from the standard 16-core version available in M5 and prior. Per Apple:

M6 also introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, providing up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations to make on-device AI workflows run even faster. System frameworks can automatically utilize both engines simultaneously, enabling applications to see faster model execution.

#2: 12-core CPU and GPU with powerful new cores

The base M6 chip offers a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU. Both are solid upgrades over the M5, which was limited to 10 cores each.

M6’s new CPU cores are especially interesting, as Apple is bringing three distinct core types to its base chip for the first time. It has 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. Here’s what Apple says about each core:

Super cores: “blaze through single-threaded workloads”

Performance cores: “use less power and join the super cores to run demanding multithreaded workloads”

Efficiency cores: “handle everyday background tasks”

Previously only M5 Pro and M5 Max—and now M5 Ultra—provided super cores and performance cores in a single chip. But now these Pro-level capabilities are available for standard M6 users. 

#3: Major efficiency gains to likely improve battery life

M6 is the first Apple chip built on a new 2nm process. And the company says that brings the benefit of “a major leap in performance and power efficiency.”

Currently the only product with an M6 is the new Mac mini, which doesn’t run on a battery.

But in the MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and other upcoming M6 products, the new chip’s “major leap” in power efficiency is likely to enable longer battery life.

Apple could always opt to shrink the physical battery to offer comparable performance as before, but here’s hoping it uses M6’s improved efficiency to deliver better battery life instead.

title: Apple has reportedly canceled innovative product that was ‘Ternus priority’
snippet: A new Omdia research note today outlined Apple’s reported Mac and iPad roadmap for the years ahead, and it also mentioned that a key rumored product has been canceled. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new Omdia research note today outlined Apple’s reported Mac and iPad roadmap for the years ahead, and it also mentioned that a key rumored product has been canceled. Here are the details.

Foldable iPad/Mac hybrid that was John Ternus ‘priority’ has reportedly been canceled

For years, rumors have suggested that the iPhone will be just the first Apple product line to adopt foldable displays.

Reporting suggests that a larger, roughly 18- or 20-inch foldable iPad/Mac hybrid device has been in the works for years. At one point it was believed to be coming as early as 2026 before later being pushed to 2028.

Earlier this year, Mark Gurman called the product a “Ternus priority” but also suggested it may never launch. He wrote:

Apple has been working on a roughly 20-inch foldable iPad. This device has been a Ternus priority but may end up being a wacky experiment that doesn’t see the light of day, according to several people who have worked on it.

You can find a good overview of prior rumors about the product here.

According to today’s Omdia report, it seems Gurman’s suspicions may have been right. It says: “product plans for 16.1-inch to 18-inch foldable MacBooks have been canceled.”

Based on prior rumors, this seems to be the same product previously covered by Gurman and others.

	

It’s very possible Apple is taking a “wait and see” approach with this foldable product as it gauges reception to the foldable iPhone Ultra. If iPhone Ultra is a hit, maybe the company will accelerate development of the iPad/MacBook hybrid.

But perhaps with the current memory crisis causing product pricing to rise so significantly already, Apple doesn’t see a current path forward for an ultra-premium, innovative foldable device like this.

title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
snippet: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."
fullText:
Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta this week after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune.

A report from the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office said that three young men set off on their hike at 3am and — although hikers are told to turn around if they haven’t reached the summit by noon — they made it to the top at 7pm. 

The trio then tried to descend in the dark, called the sheriff’s office to ask for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued the next morning by Forest Service rangers and volunteers.

While it’s not clear whether Gemini can take all the blame for these bad decisions, the sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required, especially when their planned 8-hour ascent became a multiday ordeal.”

“It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta ranger station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning,” the sheriff’s office said.

by  Terrence O'Brien

Sep 6, 2026, 8:56 PM UTC

Terrence O'Brien

 

is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

A plane bearing an Amazon logo overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday during landing, crashing into vehicles and resulting in multiple injuries. The extent of the damage or the seriousness of the injuries was not clear at the time of publication.

In the aftermath of the incident, the FAA released a statement saying:

21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway after landing at Miami International Airport around 2 p.m. local time on Sunday, Sept. 6. The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

As a result, flights at the airport were grounded and over 60 Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units were deployed to the scene. When MDFR arrived, the plane was on fire and spewing heavy smoke, according to reports. Video from the scene posted by NBC 6 (below) clearly shows the Amazon logo on the plane’s tail and thick smoke rising from the scene where the plane came to a stop on the other side of the road from the airport.

Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel told The Verge:

“We can confirm that an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air experienced an incident while attempting to land at Miami International Airport today. This is a fast-moving situation and we’re still gathering details. We’re working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We’re doing everything we can to support those affected.”

title: Apple TV’s big fall lineup: Here’s every new show and movie coming soon
snippet: Apple TV is now airing Ted Lasso season 4, and more high-profile shows and movies are coming to the streamer soon. Here’s everything in Apple TV’s fall lineup so far, which could keep growing as more premieres are announced. more…
fullText:
Apple TV is now airing Ted Lasso season 4, and more high-profile shows and movies are coming to the streamer soon. Here’s everything in Apple TV’s fall lineup so far, which could keep growing as more premieres are announced.

September

Mayday

When: September 4

What: Movie

Genre: Action-Comedy

Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh team up in “Mayday,” a genre-bending, action-packed buddy comedy that flips the spy thriller on its head. When hotshot U.S. Navy pilot Lieutenant Troy “Assassin” Kelly (Reynolds) is sent on a top-secret mission into Russian territory at the height of the Cold War, the operation implodes, leaving him stranded behind enemy lines. Discovered by Nikolai Ustinov (Branagh), a gruff ex-KGB agent with a penchant for American culture, Troy thinks he’s toast — but could an unlikely alliance between the two lead to Troy’s rescue and a bond neither saw coming?

Watch Mayday here on Apple TV

Last Seen

When: September 9

What: TV Show

Genre: Thriller

Police detective Ian Ridley’s (Patrick Brammall) life fell apart 11 years ago when his young daughter, Maggie, disappeared without a trace. Now working as a police dispatcher, the only thing that has kept him going is his implacable refusal to accept that she might be gone forever. When he receives a distress call from a teenage girl he is certain is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his broken family, whatever the cost.

Slow Horses (season 6)

When: September 16

What: TV Show

Genre: Espionage Thriller

This darkly funny espionage drama follows a team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 due to their career-ending mistakes. Led by their brilliant but irascible leader, the notorious Jackson Lamb (Academy Award winner Sir Gary Oldman), they navigate the espionage world’s smoke and mirrors to defend England from sinister forces.

Brothers

When: September 23

What: TV Show

Genre: Comedy

“Brothers” follows McConaughey and Harrelson, who play fictionalized versions of themselves, and whose lifelong friendship is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: they might actually be brothers. After Woody’s daughter’s wedding falls apart, he loads up the family and heads to Austin for an extended stay at Matthew’s ranch. But what begins as a healing getaway quickly spirals when Matthew’s mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip a long-buried secret that the two friends might actually be brothers. As Woody turns the ranch upside down in pursuit of the truth, Matthew finds himself juggling an entirely different identity crisis: a potential run for Governor of Texas. The result is a heartfelt, chaotic and wildly funny story about friendship, family, fame and the messy line between myth and reality.

October

The Last First: Winter K2

When: October 2

What: Movie

Genre: Documentary

In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that unpacks the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, mountaineers John Snorri Sigurjónsson, an Icelander, and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients and Nims, a Nepalese celebrity mountaineer, and his team of Sherpas. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life and death circumstances.

The Sisters Grimm (season 2)

When: October 2

What: TV Show

Genre: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town full of people torn straight from fantasy and fairy tales, confronting heroes and villains alike, while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. “The Sisters Grimm” blends discovery, fantasy and adventure to deliver important lessons for all ages.

Small Prophets

When: October 7

What: TV Show

Genre: Comedy

“Small Prophets” is a comic tale of the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) who, since his darling Clea disappeared seven years ago, has lived a very ordinary life. He works in a DIY store, visits his dad Brian (Sir Michael Palin) and hopes for Clea to return. One day Brian shares an old recipe involving rainwater, horse manure and more than a little alchemy. With recipe in hand, Michael sets out (albeit with some skepticism) to create homunculi — magical spirits that can predict the future — in the hope they have the answer to his burning question: “will I ever see Clea again?”

Matchbox The Movie

When: October 9

What: Movie

Genre: Action

Inspired by the iconic Mattel toys, “Matchbox The Movie” is an action-packed, globetrotting adventure about a group of friends since childhood who have their lives upended when undercover CIA agent Sean (John Cena), their long-absent former leader, returns to their small town and unwittingly gets them embroiled in a frantic international pursuit to save the world.

Tenzing

When: October 16

What: Movie

Genre: Drama

Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), was the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling.

Where’s Wanda? (season 2)

When: October 21

What: TV Show

Genre: Dark Comedy

Apple’s first German-language series “Where’s Wanda?” is a dark comedy that tells the story of Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperate to locate their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who disappeared months ago without a trace. When the police fail to find her, the family takes matters into their own hands, obtaining surveillance devices with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole. Disguising themselves as employees of an electrical company, they bug their neighborhood and then half their suburb, finding out that behind closed doors, none of their neighbors are who they pretend to be.

Nocturne

When: October 30

What: TV Show

What: Movie

Genre: Drama

They wouldn’t take Judy Heumann’s phone calls, so she took their building. In 1977, a young disabled woman (Ruth Madeley) and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. Gemini Personalization

Users can ask queries like “What’s on my calendar today?” or “Find the tracking number in my email” and receive answers tailored to their data. The feature is powered by an offline user profile and real-time online retrieval working together. 

Proactive suggestions1

Gemini Intelligence Proactive Suggestions turns complex, multi-step tasks into seamless one-tap actions in messages. If a loved one asks when is the dinner with family, Gemini automatically locates the info in your calendar and surfaces it directly on your wrist, eliminating the need to dig through your phone

Offline Gemini 

Powered by on-device AI, Gemini can process core actions instantly with low latency, even when you’re completely offline. Examples are setting up a timer, starting/stopping a workout, turning on do not disturb and other device actions.

title: Read John Ternus’s full memo to Apple employees on his first day as CEO
snippet: New Apple CEO John Ternus has just sent his first company-wide memo. In it, Ternus thanks Tim Cook and recognizes that Apple is “so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity.” “We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal,” Ternus also says, in reference to Apple’s forthcoming “Surprise and shine” special event. Read the full memo, obtained by 9to5Mac, below. more…
fullText:
New Apple CEO John Ternus has just sent his first company-wide memo. In it, Ternus thanks Tim Cook and recognizes that Apple is “so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity.”

“We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal,” Ternus also says, in reference to Apple’s forthcoming “Surprise and shine” special event.

Read the full memo, obtained by 9to5Mac, below. 

Ternus also looks further ahead in message, teasing the “incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet.”

Here is the full memo from Ternus sent to Apple employees today. 

Team,

Today, on my first day as CEO, I just wanted to send a quick note to thank everyone for the warm wishes. I also want to extend my deep appreciation to Tim for sharing so much of his knowledge and experience during this transition, and more importantly, for everything he contributed to Apple over the years. We’re so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity. We are all better for it, and I’m so grateful he’ll be our executive chairman.

I’m honored to be stepping into this role at what is truly the greatest company in the world, and I am so excited about everything we have in store. We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal. Thanks for everything you’ve all done to make it possible.

I’m just as excited about what lies beyond that, including the incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet that we’ll dream up and create together. There’s no team in the world I’d rather build the future with.

More to come. In the meantime, thanks for your excellent work!

John

title: Dell’s new 14S laptop exists to challenge MacBook Neo and, somehow, might be even cheaper
snippet: Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper. more…
fullText:
Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper.

The Dell 14S is directly positioned as an “affordable” laptop for “students, college, and everyday life.” It features an aluminum build, 21 hours of battery life, and either an Intel Core Ultra 3 or Core Ultra 5 processor. The 16:10 display has 60Hz and 120Hz options while the hardware has two USB-C ports and an HDMI port, as well as a headphone jack. 

Dell says the 14S weighs in at around 2.5lbs and is just 13.5mm thick. 

In a Q&A on its blog, Dell directly positions the 14S as a “compelling” alternative to the MacBook Neo, though pricing hasn’t actually been announced at this point. The company hints, though, that it will be cheaper than the XPS 13 that already starts at $699 – in other words, Dell 14S might just be cheaper than the MacBook Neo.

	

The Dell 14S is available in the United States this fall. Pricing will be announced closer to availability in each market. What we can say is that the Dell 14S is designed to be complementary to XPS 13 and accessible for students and young adults globally. We’re committed to making sure regional pricing reflects that too.

Amusingly, Dell acknowledges that it already launched a laptop called the “14S” earlier this year, saying that the “old” one is designed for creators, while this “new” model “prioritizes everyday performance, long battery life, portability, colorful design and accessible pricing.” Perfectly not confusing.

fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro will be unveiled next week, and a new post from a reputable Weibo leaker names three new colors expected to debut.

Next week at its September event, Apple will reveal all the details of its new flagship iPhone models.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will launch alongside iPhone Ultra. And rumors have revealed a lot of what to expect already.

Colors always seem like one of the last details to be finalized by Apple. But this year, consensus has largely pointed to a Dark Cherry/Burgundy as the flagship replacement for Cosmic Orange, plus a new Silver and a Sky Blue. 

Reports have conflicted on whether Apple will have a Black/Space Gray model this year.

But a new post from Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital points to a slightly different color lineup. He predicts:

Dark Cherry/Burgundy

Sky Blue

Black

The leaker says Silver will “most likely” not be available, adding in a follow-up post that he’s seen no evidence of the model coming. And if this lineup proves accurate, that means Apple is replacing the full roster of iPhone 17 Pro colors with all-new options for iPhone 18 Pro.

Sky Blue has been used for iPhone Air and MacBook Air before, and in both cases the blue is very subtle. In everyday lighting it appears more like a silver finish. So it’s possible Apple is banking on Sky Blue being a good replacement for shoppers who prefer Silver.

Many users were disappointed last year that there was no Black or Space Gray option of iPhone 17 Pro. So here’s hoping this latest leak proves true and Black returns in iPhone 18 Pro.
